 RBI Retains Rs 50,000 Cash NEFT Limit Under New Domestic Money Transfer Rules 
 National News Economy RBI Retains Rs 50,000 Cash NEFT Limit Under New Domestic Money Transfer Rules
 Edited By : Ameya Sathaye Published : November 12, 2026, 11:03 AM IST   |   Updated : November 12, 2026, 11:04 AM IST   |   0 
 Share 0 
 The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has issued consolidated directions on domestic money transfers, retaining the Rs 50,000 cash NEFT limit for walk-in customers without bank accounts. The framework also maintains transaction and monthly limits for transfers through business correspondents and other channels while strengthening safeguards against suspicious transactions.
 Key Highlights
 RBI retains the Rs 50,000 cash NEFT limit for walk-in customers without bank accounts.
 Cash transfers through business correspondents, ATMs and other permitted channels are capped at Rs 5,000 per transaction and Rs 25,000 per remitter per month.
 Cash payouts to beneficiaries without bank accounts are limited to Rs 10,000 per transaction and Rs 25,000 per beneficiary per month.
 Banks and payment service providers must strengthen transaction monitoring, customer alerts and reporting of suspicious activity.
 RBI Issues Consolidated Domestic Money Transfer Directions
 New Delhi, Nov 12: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has issued a consolidated set of directions governing domestic money transfer services, retaining existing transaction limits while strengthening safeguards for cash-based remittances.
 The framework covers transfers made by customers who do not have bank accounts at the branch where they initiate transactions, as well as other permitted domestic money transfer facilities.
 Under the directions, walk-in customers without an account at a bank branch can transfer up to Rs 50,000 in cash through NEFT into a bank account.
 The central bank has retained the existing limits for transfers through business correspondents, ATMs and other permitted channels.
 Transaction Limits for Cash-Based Money Transfers
 The RBI framework specifies limits for both cash deposits into beneficiary accounts and cash payouts to beneficiaries who do not hold bank accounts.
 Type of transaction Transaction limit Monthly limit 
 Cash NEFT by walk-in customers Rs 50,000 As specified under the applicable framework 
 Transfers through business correspondents, ATMs and other permitted channels Rs 5,000 Rs 25,000 per remitter 
 Cash payouts to beneficiaries without bank accounts Rs 10,000 Rs 25,000 per beneficiary 
 For cash payouts, banks can facilitate transfers from customers’ accounts through ATMs, business correspondents and other authorised payment channels.
 According to the RBI, these limits were part of the earlier framework and have been retained in the consolidated directions.
 Remitter Verification and Transaction Identification
 The central bank has retained the requirement for remitter registration using a verified mobile number and a self-certified officially valid document, as prescribed under the RBI’s Know Your Customer Directions, 2025.
 Remitting banks and business correspondents must also ensure that remitter details are included in the IMPS or NEFT transaction message.
 The transaction message must carry an identifier that distinguishes cash-based remittances from other transfers. This will help improve traceability and monitoring of transactions.
 RBI Strengthens Monitoring and Fraud Prevention Safeguards
 The new directions require banks and non-bank entities to establish safeguards, including transaction velocity checks and alerts to customers about credits received through domestic money transfer facilities.
 Banks and other regulated entities must immediately investigate unusual increases in the volume of credits in an individual account or a group of accounts. Suspicious transactions must be reported to the appropriate authorities.
 The framework also requires fund transfers to be effected on a real-time or near-real-time basis. Inter-bank settlement must take place only through payment systems approved by the RBI.
 Entities Covered Under the New Directions
 The consolidated directions apply to all scheduled commercial banks, including:
 Regional Rural Banks
 Urban Co-operative Banks
 State Co-operative Banks
 District Central Co-operative Banks
 They also cover authorised payment system operators and participants to the extent that the directions apply to their domestic money transfer services.
 However, card-to-card transfers have been excluded from the scope of the directions.
 The RBI’s consolidated domestic money transfer framework retains existing cash transaction limits while placing greater emphasis on customer verification, transaction traceability and monitoring of suspicious activity. The measures aim to strengthen safeguards across domestic remittance channels without changing the specified limits for cash-based transfers.
